A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework, renamed from ThinkVideo to CoT-RVS. Text, equations, figures, tables, and all appendices are readable and matchable despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation results, keyframe ablations, and qualitative offline and online experiments in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original segmentation experiments and additionally reports component costs, end-to-end efficiency comparisons, and output-format reliability measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same keyframe selector, image segmenter, video processor, overlap removal, and online update procedure. The offline and online prompts in Appendices A–B are identical. The temporal-semantic terminology expands the explanation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MeViS, Refer-DAVIS-17, ReasonVOS, ReVOS, and T-ReasonVOS, retaining offline, online, instance-level, and temporally sensitive scenarios. Appendix D retains the same 45-video, 180-pair T-ReasonVOS subset. Added analyses remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds SAMWISE to Tables 1–2 and GLUS to Tables 1, 3, and 4. Figure 2 adds a VISA keyframe comparison, and Table A2 compares efficiency with VideoLISA. The relocated panda example drops its Seg-Zero and ThinkFirst comparisons; other established quantitative comparators remain.

E3.justification: New Appendices F–G introduce resource measurements using 324-sized frames and eight keyframe candidates, plus a per-expression valid-output metric for selector evaluation. Existing segmentation settings remain unchanged. Neither PDF explains whether the revised MeViS scores reflect a split or protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendices F–G substantially extend diagnostic evidence with component and end-to-end cost analyses and systematic quantification of previously discussed output-format failures. Figure 2 adds a temporal keyframe-selection case. Existing keyframe-count and CoT ablations remain, and v2 Table 7 survives as v3 Table A3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Table A4's new valid-output percentages are evaluation metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the LLaVA, Gemma3, and GPT-4o J&F scores from 52.5, 52.6, and 60.1 with 45.9, 44.2, and 52.2. The earlier Gemma3/GPT-4o values reappear under MeViS val_u in Table A4, leaving same-setting comparability unresolved. New baseline, cost, reliability, and qualitative results expand the evidence; matched scores in Tables 2–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix F newly introduces an approximate average online latency expression and derives its upper bound from selector, segmentation, and tracking costs. The task definitions and main Equations 1–12 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim training-free, zero-shot CoT segmentation, instance-level outputs, online target updating, and superiority on explicit and implicit queries. v3 foregrounds temporal-semantic keyframe selection in its contribution list without changing these capabilities or their application scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly acknowledges computational expense as a tradeoff of complex CoT reasoning. Appendix G interprets output-format validity as evidence for more reliable reasoning with larger closed-source models. Existing limitations concerning pretrained-model capability, grouped instances, ambiguous queries, and inadequate benchmarks are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds resource-measurement details, memory and API-cost information, and a reproducibility statement specifying code and data release upon acceptance. The advertised repository changes to CoT-RVS. Existing prompts, pretrained components, GPT-4o version, core hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Guo et al. (2022), Hu et al. (2023), Lian et al. (2023), Lin et al. (2025, GLUS), and Snell et al. (2024), connecting the work to modular pretrained-model use and test-time computation. The established research positioning remains; SAMWISE was already cited in v2.

P1.justification: v3 renames the paper and framework, revises the abstract and parts of the introduction and contribution list, expands temporal-semantic explanations, and adopts author-year citations. The main section sequence and most method, experimental, and existing appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template and typography throughout and substantially rearranges figure and table placement. It adds Figure 2 and three appendix tables, relocates Table 7 to A3, and reformats the panda example into Figure A7 with additional frames and fewer comparators.

improvement.justification: Added baselines and cost/reliability analyses improve scrutiny of the framework. However, v3 leaves the revised MeViS scores unexplained, mixes 785- and 458-expression denominators within Table A4's ReasonVOS rows, and retains 15.6% referring and 18% reasoning improvement claims that no longer match the updated best offline baselines. These reporting problems undermine the added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
